column1: # lesson-symptoms.tsv — the symptom-to-lesson table read by hooks/lib/lesson_recall.py
# (truememory-2026-09-27.md §3.6 step 3, item #6). A Bash result or a PostToolUseFailure `.error`
# containing a literal below gets a one-line POINTER to the lesson, never the lesson text.
# FORMAT: literal<TAB>pointer<TAB>note. `#` lines are comments. At most 15 rows; past that, move to
# the `symptoms:` frontmatter + compile cache the design defers (§3.6 last bullet).
#   literal  12+ chars, matched case-sensitively as a substring. It must come from a FOREIGN
#            emitter (git, bash, shellcheck, bats, jq, sqlite, nohup) and be verbatim in the lesson
#            body or its incident. SEED RULE: a literal printed by one of OUR scripts would make the
#            table fire on itself, so tests/lesson-recall.bats refuses any literal `git grep -F`
#            finds on a non-comment line of bin/ scripts/ hooks/.
#   pointer  docs/lessons/<slug>.md (repo-relative, resolved against the dereferenced repo root at
#            runtime) or ~/.claude/projects/<key>/memory/<slug>.md (`~` expands to $HOME). The
#            basename minus `.md` is the slug that dedup, holdout and lesson-hits.jsonl key on.
#   note     for humans; never rendered.
# PRECISION over recall: a noisy pointer trains the model to ignore all of them. Dropped 2026-09-28:
# `cannot lock ref` (the memory is about the remote `… is at X but expected Y` lost race, and a
# substring cannot separate that from a local ref collision). Reads of the lesson corpus itself are
# skipped by the scan (lesson_recall.READ_OF_CORPUS), or every lesson read would point at itself.
# This file is never linked live (install.sh links only *.sh and *.py), so the hooks resolve it
# through their dereferenced self-path (acceptance X1).
